subject: POC trial planning & workload intake - Acme Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: POC goals & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can kick off the POC: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: patient intake form summarization + risk-scoring for triage workflows.
- Success criteria: >= 92% recall on high-risk flags across the evaluation set, median inference latency < 120ms at 50 RPS, and acceptable cost per 1k tokens compared to current provider.
- Data constraints: PHI in transcripts — customer will confirm data isolation & preferred retention window.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
1) Week 0 (this week): Share workload profile and baseline sample data (you) + Redwood provides preliminary capacity sizing and proposal.
2) Week 1: Redwood spins up POC cluster (Dedicated trial) and shares test endpoints.
3) Week 2: Run partner tests (acme test harness) — collect metrics and qualitative checks.
4) Week 3: Joint review of results, decide next steps/rollout.

Workload intake we need from you (attached template):
- Expected average RPS and peak bursts (per region)
- Typical prompt/token lengths (input vs. response)
- Concurrency and burst patterns (time-of-day, batching)
- Sample payloads (anonymized) and SLO thresholds

Next steps: can you confirm you’ll share the completed workload_profile.xlsx by EOD Friday (Apr 2)? I’ll follow up with a proposed POC SOW and target dates.

Attachments: acme_workload_profile.xlsx (template)

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

----
On Tue, 30 Mar 2027 at 14:30 Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben & team — good call. Will pull sample data and the intake template.
> 
> Alice
> Director of Clinical Automation | Acme Health
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: POC goals & next steps (Acme Health)

Thanks Ben —

We’ll get the workload profile filled out. Quick answers to some items from the call: 
- Avg RPS: 35 (US-East), typical sustained 20 RPS with scheduled peaks up to 120 RPS for ~10–15 minutes during clinic check-ins.
- Token lengths: inputs average 220 tokens, responses ~60 tokens. Some long intake notes can reach 1,200 tokens but those are <1% of traffic.
- Concurrency: expected 50 concurrent sessions during peak; they’re currently batching some intake forms at the edge but would prefer per-request latency under 200ms.

We’ll share anonymized sample payloads and the completed workload_profile.xlsx by Friday. Raj (CTO) is looped for procurement alignment.

Best,
Alice
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: POC goals & next steps (Acme Health)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Alice — this is super helpful. A couple clarifying Qs so our sizing is accurate: 
1) For the 120 RPS burst, does that reflect sustained per second requests or batched requests that will arrive as a small number of large requests? (i.e., will we see 120 individual inference calls/sec or 120 calls in 10-second bursts?)
2) For the <1% long notes (~1,200 tokens), are those processed synchronously in the same path as the shorter inputs or via an async pipeline?

If you prefer, we can set up a 20-min follow-up tomorrow to confirm and walk the team through the intake template. Otherwise we’ll size conservatively for 120 RPS sustained bursts and surface any cost/latency implications.

I’ve attached a preliminary POC SOW (redwood_poc_sow_v2.pdf) that outlines roles/responsibilities and ownership for test runs.

Thanks —
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: POC sizing notes (Acme)

Ben — quick internal note before we finalize sizing:
- If bursts are truly 120 RPS sustained for 10–15 minutes, recommend reserved Dedicated nodes (2x A10g equiv) for the trial to keep latency < 120ms at target tokens.
- Plan for KV/prefix caching for common prompts to reduce token cost — ask Acme about caching tolerances (staleness).
- For long-tail 1,200-token requests, enable async fallback so synchronous SLAs aren’t impacted; measure separately in evaluation.

I’ll draft the concrete sizing numbers by EOD and add to the SOW.

—Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: POC goals & next steps (Acme Health)

Alice / Raj —

Thanks for the details — and thanks for looping procurement. Quick confirmation and next steps so everyone has clarity: 

Confirmed from Acme:
- Avg RPS (US-East): 35; peak bursts up to 120 RPS (10–15 minutes).
- Typical tokens: input ~220, response ~60; long-tail <1% at ~1,200 tokens, processed synchronously.

Redwood proposed actions:
- We’ll size the POC for 120 RPS bursts and include a short-lived burst buffer (Dedicated reserved capacity) to meet latency SLOs. Marissa is building the concrete node-level sizing and cost estimate.
- Enable prefix caching for common prompts; we’ll surface caching TTL tradeoffs for Acme to approve.
- Long requests: we recommend routing >1,000-token requests to a separate async worker to avoid latency impact; if Acme requires synchronous handling for those, we’ll note the cost/latency delta in the POC report.

Deliverables & ownership:
- Acme: completed workload_profile.xlsx + anonymized sample payloads (Alice) — due EOD Friday, Apr 2.
- Redwood: POC SOW (Ben) & sizing estimate (Marissa) — will share by Mon, Apr 5.
- Joint: test plan & success-metrics doc (call out recall/latency/cost) — targeted for Wed, Apr 7 review.

Let me know if this matches your expectations. If so I’ll send the DocuSign SOW and schedule the kickoff for Apr 6.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_poc_sow_v2.pdf]
